angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families, tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; last season's SOE as a day-3 lean (WR only) with GO/HOLD calls tied to a rule-picked film checklist.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 unseen classes; best case +1.0 in (0.14 catches) inside the pre-set +/-3 in margin (0.44 catches). Baseline held-out R2 0.00 [-0.51, 0.14] (ridge 0.03 [-0.28, 0.14]), RMSE 8.6 in. Speed benchmark: 40 vs full-play NFL top speed 0.43 within position and class; drill cut to same NFL route 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32]. Last-season SOE gain over pick+routes: 53 pairs 0.33 [0.13, 0.53]; day 3 (20 pairs) 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], leave-one-pair-out 0.19 to 0.37, season-fold shuffle p 0.01; WR 0.56 [-0.02, 0.99], TE -0.50 [-1.12, 0.00]. Earlier lists 7/13 (54% [32, 75]) vs base 8/20 (40% [24, 58]), intervals overlap.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_17/cand_2. Football: GO reworded to a lean ('if you must choose between two day-3 receivers...') and made conditional on a rule-picked film checklist with 3 named 2025 clips per GO player (hitch sink, slant/out at speed, best snap vs man; Douglas's sampled hitch flagged as no sink) and an explicit flip rule (no sink on full tape or 2026 SOE < 0 after 150 routes); the pooled 53-pair gain shown beside the day-3 gain as the main evidence; slot share and position in the shortlist, with a statement that 20 pairs cannot separate slot from wide; WR vs TE gains both reported (new action: WR only); one margin (+1.0 in / 0.14 catches inside the pre-set +/-3 in) and one speed benchmark (0.43) in lede and body; the three speed windows moved to one labelled appendix table; one-sided p, TOST, split-half, shuffle-p rows and the hitch-sink hypothesis removed. Data science: one sentence names the estimand and season-pair folds and explains the earlier 0.63 (leave-one-receiver-out folds where the baseline scored -0.43); leave-one-pair-out gains for all 20 pairs plotted against the season-fold permutation null (p 0.01); TE-only gain with interval; ridge baseline R2; baseline_inputs.csv + soe_season.csv + reproduce_baseline.py re-derive R2 0.00, RMSE 8.6 and slope -1.2 from data/processed in seconds (run and asserted at the end of analysis.py); numbers.json now holds exactly the keys the text uses (p1/pc1 duplication gone); pre-registered flip rule with power 0.27 / 0.20. Writeup: jargon replaced ('about 60% signal and 40% noise'), motivation split into evidence problem and speed benchmark; headings renamed to findings; Watch list and power paragraph moved out, one-line 'what would change the call'; base-rate comparison identical in table and text. Viz: Fig 1A scatter with rugs, fitted line and 90% band, five labelled; 1B gap at the turn marked on each panel, fonts >= 11 pt; Fig 2 power as marker size, no repeated column; Fig 3 difference row with band and outlined ribbons; Fig 4 rebuilt as paired contrast (WR/TE labelled), leave-one-pair-out with permutation band, gain and hit-rate interval strips (7/13 vs 6/13 vs 8/20), larger 2026 cards. check.py: 1,967 words, 4 figures + 4 tables.
open_risks: The day-3 edge is still not proven: the bootstrap interval includes zero, draft-class folds halve the gain (0.15), and the rule barely beats raw last-season SOE (0.09 [-0.19, 0.40]); the permutation p (0.01) and the bootstrap tell different stories and a judge may ask why.
The WR-only recommendation was made after seeing the TE split (5 TE pairs, gain -0.50); it is a post-hoc restriction.
Film clips are drawn from a sample of up to 40 snaps per player (half top-EPA); Douglas has 9 sampled 2025 snaps and a single hitch, so his checklist rests on very few reps.
GO/HOLD rule and the flip rule were set after seeing the history; the freeze date (24 October 2026) is after the 2026 season began, and the 2026 tests have power 0.27 (gain) and 0.20 (list).
Fig 4 is tall (four panels); judges may still find it dense at column width.
